opening.title: Why bioinformatics is essential to advanced molecular pathology
opening.lead: Turning complex molecular data into reliable evidence for diagnosis, prognosis and therapy.
opening.question: But how does our role differ from that of molecular biologists?
opening.start: A shared effort. A clearer answer.

challenge.title: A molecular test is more than a sequencer
challenge.lead: Advanced testing connects laboratory work, computational analysis and clinical context.
challenge.callout: More data does not automatically mean more certainty. The analytical path must be controlled, transparent and fit for purpose.

need.title: Complex data needs a dependable interpreter
need.lead: We help turn raw output into evidence that can be reviewed, reproduced and used responsibly.
need.card1-copy: High-throughput assays produce far more measurements than can be assessed manually, consistently or quickly.
need.card2-title: Know when not to trust a call
need.card2-copy: Quality checks, coverage review and artifact awareness help distinguish a plausible finding from a technical false signal.
need.card3-copy: Annotation and curated knowledge help place findings in biological and clinical context for expert review.
need.card4-copy: Versioned, validated workflows support reproducibility, auditability and consistent results over time.
need.bottom-line: Our contribution: reliable analysis—not an automated diagnosis.

workflow.title: Build a path from raw reads to reviewable findings
workflow.lead: Each stage adds checks and context; each stage can also introduce uncertainty.
workflow.stage1-copy: Map reads and check sample-level quality.
workflow.stage2-copy: Identify variants or other assay-specific signals.
workflow.stage3-copy: Review depth, quality and potential artifacts.
workflow.stage4-copy: Relate findings to genes, disease and knowledge sources.
workflow.stage5-copy: Present traceable evidence for expert interpretation.
workflow.note: Bioinformatics supports the diagnostic team. Clinical interpretation and reporting remain governed by qualified professionals and local procedures.

roles.title: Where our work differs—and where it meets
roles.lead: A useful distinction is the main problem each role is trained to solve.
roles.lab-title: Makes the assay work in the lab
roles.lab-point1: Develops, performs and optimizes laboratory methods
roles.lab-point2: Works with specimens, extraction, reagents and instruments
roles.lab-point3: Monitors controls, assay performance and wet-lab causes of failure
roles.bio-point1: Builds, validates and maintains computational workflows
roles.bio-point2: Assesses data quality, analytical limits and potential artifacts
roles.bio-point3: Adds annotations and makes results reproducible and traceable
roles.shared-copy: validate the complete test, investigate discordant results and improve quality across the whole pathway.

together.title: One finding. Two complementary lenses.
together.lead: Example: a low-frequency variant appears in a tumour sequencing panel.
together.lab-question: Could the sample or assay explain this signal?
together.lab-copy: Review sample quality, assay controls, library preparation and known method limitations.
together.bio-question: Is the signal supported by the data and pipeline?
together.bio-copy: Review read-level evidence, depth, quality metrics, artifact flags and workflow behavior.
together.team-label: THE TEAM, INCLUDING THE PATHOLOGIST, THEN
together.team-copy: Weighs the technical evidence, biological context and clinical question before conclusions are reported.

takeaway.title: Different expertise. One dependable result.
takeaway.why-copy: To process complex molecular data with validated, quality-aware and reproducible analysis—and make the evidence reviewable.
takeaway.difference-copy: Molecular biologists focus on the biological assay and its laboratory performance. Bioinformaticians focus on the computational workflow and its analytical performance.
takeaway.closing: Neither role replaces the other—or the pathologist’s clinical judgment. The strongest result comes from the full team.
